status: agreed with Eduard 26 Oct 2026; recognition confirmed from real letters 28 Oct 2026
inherits_note: Uses the same questions, reasons, routes, not-filed choice, deadline checks, late-appeal question, not-accepted options and SA370 output as sa-late-filing-100. Only the differences are listed here.

applies_to_tax_years.note: From 2026-27, clients in Making Tax Digital for Income Tax may come under the points-based late submission regime instead. Separate rule to be added.

recognition.amount_rule: £10 a day, up to £900; the letter shows the number of days or the period charged
recognition.line_on_page_2: 3 months late - a daily penalty of £10 a day for a maximum of 90 days
recognition.legal_reference: Paragraph 4 of Schedule 55 to the Finance Act 2009

facts_for_explanation.what_it_is: Because your return was more than 3 months late, HMRC charges £10 for each day it stayed late, for up to 90 days (a maximum of £900).
points: The daily penalties stop once 90 days have been charged.
They are on top of the £100 penalty you may already have received.

recognition.amount_rule: 5% of the tax due or £300, whichever is greater
recognition.line_on_page_2: 6 months late - you have been charged the minimum filing penalty of £300 (or 5% of the tax due)
recognition.legal_reference: Paragraph 5 of Schedule 55 to the Finance Act 2009

facts_for_explanation.what_it_is: Because your return was more than 6 months late, HMRC charges a further penalty of 5% of the tax due or £300, whichever is greater.
points: If your return isn't filed yet, HMRC estimates the tax you owe and bases this penalty on that estimate.
Filing your return replaces the estimate and may lower this penalty.

recognition.amount_rule: Another 5% of the tax due or £300, whichever is greater
recognition.legal_reference: Paragraph 6 of Schedule 55 to the Finance Act 2009 (expected; not yet seen in a sample)

facts_for_explanation.what_it_is: Because your return was more than 12 months late, HMRC charges another penalty of 5% of the tax due or £300, whichever is greater.
points: If HMRC believes information was deliberately withheld, this penalty can be much higher.

checks.if: penalty_amount > max(300, 5% of tax due shown on the letter)

case_grouping.note: All late filing penalties for the same tax year (including the £100 penalty) go on one SA370, which has a section for each penalty.

routing_reminders: Penalties over £100 follow the normal route (decided 25 Oct 2026).
More than one tax year: call-back only.
Each penalty notice has its own 30-day appeal deadline from its own date; the app shows the earliest.

heading_phrases: Late filing penalties for the year ended
recognition_common.source: Confirmed from real HMRC letters supplied by Eduard, 28 Oct 2026

extra_lines: If you have recently filed a tax return, we will send you a revised penalty assessment shortly.
You will also have to pay interest on all outstanding amounts, including penalties.

extended_appeal_date_on_letter.rule: If page 2 of the notice says 'We've given you more time to appeal your penalty. You now have until [date]', use that date as the appeal deadline instead of notice date + 30 days.
extended_appeal_date_on_letter.phrase: We've given you more time to appeal your penalty
